EQUITY: Machinery and Equipment
Industry upcycle meets operational improvement
Well positioned to benefit from domestic upcycle, overseas expansion and mining machinery momentum
Initiate at Buy with a TP of CNY13.60, implying 39.5% upside

Considering China's construction machinery upcycle, the company's continued overseas expansion and the accelerating growth in its mining machinery business, we forecast the company's revenue and net profit to grow at CAGRs of \(13.5\%\) and \(28.7\%\) over 2026-28F, respectively. We value the company at 18x 2026F P/E, broadly in line with the peer average. Based on our 2026F EPS of CNY0.76, we derive a TP of CNY13.60. The stock has declined \(5.3\%\) over the past month as of 29 May, underperforming the CSI 300 by 7.0pp. We believe this reflects market preference for technology-related themes rather than weakening fundamentals. The stock currently trades around 13x 2026F P/E, below the peer average. However, with industry beta improving and XCMG's company-specific alpha becoming more visible, we believe XCMG offers long-term investment value, making the current price level attractive. Key catalysts include continued y-y improvement in domestic monthly industry data and stronger mining machinery demand supported by higher commodity prices and mining capex. Key downside risks include changes in the competitive landscape, weaker-than-expected R&D capabilities, slower mining machinery expansion, softer downstream demand, geopolitical and overseas operating risks, raw material price volatility and FX volatility risk.

Industry beta: Domestic recovery and overseas expansion to drive earnings visibility
We believe China's construction machinery industry is transitioning from an export-led phase to a more balanced growth phase supported by domestic cyclical recovery and continued overseas expansion. In China, policy support, equipment replacement demand and electrification/green transition trends should drive a new upcycle, while overseas expansion still offers a growth runway for Chinese players. According to Frost & Sullivan (via Sany Heavy Industry's post-hearing information pack), overseas markets account for over 80% of global construction machinery sales. Yet, top Chinese OEMs held only a c.12% overseas share in 2024, by our estimates, suggesting significant room for penetration. Against this backdrop, we expect XCMG to benefit from both domestic recovery and global share gains. Based on our industry growth and market share assumptions, we forecast 2026-28F revenue CAGRs of 17.8%/8.0%/12.0% for XCMG's earthmoving/hoisting/concrete machinery businesses.
Company alpha: Mining machinery and SOE reform to unlock growth potential

According to XCMG's investor relations activity record, the company targets mining machinery revenue of more than CNY40bn by 2030. We view mining machinery as one of XCMG's most differentiated businesses and a potential second growth engine, poised to lift overall gross margin. Furthermore, we see SOE reform as an important driver of better operating quality. XCMG has followed a reform path of “mixed-ownership reform and strategic capital introduction, group-level listing and equity incentives”, which closely aligns management and shareholder interests. We believe the company's targets on ROE and operating cash flow will encourage a higher revenue contribution from overseas markets and high-end products, and accelerate the exit of underperforming assets. Over time, this should support both earnings quality and valuation re-rating, in our view.

Company profile

XCMG is a leading company in China's construction machinery industry. The company has a comprehensive product portfolio covering hoisting machinery, earthmoving machinery, concrete machinery, road machinery, aerial work platforms, mining machinery, agricultural machinery, and other major product categories, enabling it to serve a wide range of construction and engineering scenarios.
Valuation Methodology

Based on an 18x target P/E, broadly in line with the average of comparable companies, and our 2026F EPS of CNY0.76, we derive a target price of CNY13.60. The stock's benchmark index is the CSI 300 Index.
Risks that may impede the achievement of the target price

Key downside risks include changes in the global and regional competitive landscape, weaker-than-expected R&D capabilities, slower-than-expected mining machinery business expansion, lower-than-expected downstream demand in China and overseas markets, a complex global operating environment and geopolitical risks, raw material price volatility, and FX volatility.
ESG

XCMG has continued to advance the development of distributed PV projects. According to the company's 2025 ESG report, by end-2025, its cumulative installed clean energy capacity had reached 189.17MW, with annual power generation totaling 180mn kWh and green electricity accounting for \(20.45\%\) of total electricity consumption. During the year, the company added approximately 54MW of distributed PV capacity, which is expected to generate more than 54mn kWh of electricity annually and reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 5,380 tonnes per year.

Investment highlights
Results review

XCMG released its 2025 annual results and 1Q26 results in Apr 2026. In 2025, the company delivered revenue of CNY100,823mn, up 8.37% y-y, and net profit of CNY6,572mn, up 8.96% y-y. Weighted average ROE was 11.0%, up 0.63pp y-y. In 1Q26, XCMG recorded revenue of CNY29,791mn, up 9.26% y-y, and net profit of CNY2,056mn, up 0.86% y-y. 1Q net profit growth lagged revenue growth, mainly because exchange rate volatility drove financial expenses from a net gain of CNY113mn in the same period last year to a net expense of CNY691mn, in our view.
Gearing up: Industry upcycle meets operational improvement

From an industry beta perspective, we believe China's construction machinery industry is transitioning from an export-led phase to a more balanced growth phase supported by domestic cyclical recovery and continued overseas expansion. In China, policy support, equipment replacement demand, and rising electrification penetration are all likely to drive a cyclical recovery, providing more stable demand support for Chinese construction machinery manufacturers. Meanwhile, overseas expansion still offers a growth runway for Chinese players, supported by strong product value-for-money, efficient supply chains, and improving localized operating capabilities, in our view.

Beyond industry beta, we believe XCMG's company-specific alpha is also becoming increasingly visible. On the business front, the company continues to optimize its product and revenue mix. Mining machinery is one of XCMG's most differentiated segments and has the potential to become a second growth driver, given its high technological barriers, robust margins, and strong customer stickiness. According to XCMG's investor relations activity record dated 14 Feb 2026, management targets mining machinery revenue of more than CNY40bn by 2030, underscoring a clear long-term strategic commitment for the business. On governance, after the advancement of SOE reform, XCMG has stepped up efforts to improve asset quality, including the clean-up of accounts receivable and inventories. This has enhanced operating quality and risk resilience, and should help the company convert revenue growth into profit growth more efficiently, in our view. On incentives, the company released its equity incentive plan in Dec 2025, incorporating ROE and operating cash flow into its core performance assessment metrics. We believe this reflects management's focus on high-quality profit growth. Overall, we believe the optimization of XCMG's business structure, improvement in governance mechanisms, and stronger incentive discipline should jointly support its company-specific alpha. The stock offers attractive medium- to long-term allocation value, in our view.
Industry outlook: Domestic cyclical recovery and overseas expansion to drive demand growth

Before 2021, XCMG's revenue trend was highly correlated with China's domestic machinery cycle. However, as the company expanded overseas, its sensitivity to the domestic cycle declined, revenue volatility moderated, and its growth drivers gradually shifted from domestic demand alone to a combination of domestic and overseas demand. Looking back at XCMG's revenue trend and excavator industry sales volume data over 2012-2025, the company's revenue showed clear cyclical patterns during 2012-2021. However, during the industry downturn in 2022-2024, XCMG's revenue remained relatively resilient. We believe this was mainly due to the continued increase in its overseas revenue contribution, which rose from \(29.67\%\) in 2022 to \(48.20\%\) in 2025.

At the current stage, we believe improving industry beta remains the core driver of XCMG's revenue growth. Compared with the previous cycle, however, this round of industry growth should be more balanced: the domestic market is in a cyclical recovery phase, while overseas markets continue to expand. Based on industry data estimated by Frost & Sullivan and cited in Sany Heavy Industry's post-hearing information pack, together with our assessment of XCMG's business mix and industry trends, we estimate the company's domestic and overseas revenue and gross profit contributions for 2026-2027 to analyze how changes in industry demand may affect its revenue growth and profitability.

We assess XCMG's demand outlook through two lenses: China's cyclical recovery, which should support domestic volume growth, and overseas expansion, which should provide both revenue upside and margin improvement.
China market: domestic demand recovery marks the start of a new construction machinery upcycle

We believe China's construction machinery industry is in the early stage of a cyclical recovery. Given the cyclical nature of the sector, excavator sales volume remains one of the most widely followed indicators of construction machinery demand. The previous upcycle started in 2016, driven by improving infrastructure investment, equipment replacement demand, deeper implementation of the Belt and Road Initiative, and the upgrade to China III emission standards. China's excavator sales volume reached a peak of 343k units in 2021.

Since May 2021, however, the industry entered a downcycle as downstream investment demand weakened. From an equipment replacement perspective, construction machinery products typically have a replacement cycle of 8-10 years. We therefore believe the industry is now at the starting point of a new upcycle. Since April 2024, monthly excavator sales have returned to positive y-y growth and remained positive for 22 consecutive months through January 2026. Excavator sales volume declined y-y in February 2026 due to the Chinese New Year holiday, but returned to positive y-y growth in March and April.

According to the China Construction Machinery Association, total industry excavator sales volume reached 102,100 units in 4M26, up 22.2% y-y. Domestic sales volume rose 15.0% y-y to 56,500 units, while exports increased 32.5% y-y to 45,600 units. In a typical construction cycle, demand for cranes and concrete machinery tends to follow earthmoving equipment with a lag. Given the recovery is already visible in earthmoving machinery, we believe hoisting machinery and concrete machinery are also likely to enter a bottoming-out and recovery phase.

Overall, we believe China's construction machinery industry is entering a new upcycle. In our view, policy support and major projects - including urban renewal, hydropower projects in the lower reaches of the Yarlung Zangbo River, the new round of rural road upgrade initiatives, additional special treasury bonds, and ultra-long-term treasury bonds - should provide fresh momentum for an accelerating recovery in construction machinery demand. We also believe electrification, green transition, and equipment replacement demand will help the domestic construction machinery industry move out of its trough and support a recovery in domestic sales.

According to Frost & Sullivan estimates cited in Sany Heavy Industry's post-hearing information pack, China's construction machinery market reached USD26.9bn in sales value in 2025, and is expected to expand to USD36.5bn in 2026 and USD50.6bn in 2028, implying a 2026-28 CAGR of \(23.4\%\), ahead of Asia-Pacific ex-China, Europe, North America, Latin America and Africa over the same period. China's share of global construction machinery sales is also expected to rise from \(15.2\%\) in 2025 to \(18.1\%\) in 2028.

In terms of the competitive landscape, we believe domestic demand recovery should mainly benefit leading domestic OEMs. Based on the 2025 domestic revenue of four leading Chinese OEMs - XCMG (000425 CH, Buy), Sany Heavy Industry (600031 CH, Buy), Zoomlion (000157 CH, Not Rated), and LiuGong (000528 CH, Not Rated) - together with Frost & Sullivan's estimates for China's construction machinery market sales value, we estimate that these four leading companies together accounted for c.67% of the domestic market in 2025. Among them, XCMG had one of the largest domestic revenue bases, with an estimated domestic market share of c.28.4%.

By product, we believe the four leading domestic OEMs each have distinct competitive strengths. In earthmoving machinery, Sany Heavy Industry remains the domestic leader. The consolidation of excavator assets has made earthmoving machinery one of XCMG's core segments, and the company has been steadily narrowing the gap with the market leader. In hoisting machinery, XCMG, Zoomlion, and Sany Heavy Industry dominate the domestic market, with XCMG holding a leading position in products such as truck cranes and truck-mounted cranes. In mining machinery, XCMG has further strengthened its competitive advantage in complete and series-based product offerings following the integration of industrial assets such as wide-body dump trucks, enabling it to compete directly with Caterpillar (CAT US) and Komatsu (6301 JP). As the current upcycle is being driven by policy support, replacement demand and electrification / green transition trends, we expect leading domestic OEMs with broader product portfolios and stronger integrated capabilities to be better positioned to deliver excess returns.

Overseas markets: global share gains to open room for profitability improvement

According to Frost & Sullivan estimates cited in Sany Heavy Industry's post-hearing information pack, overseas markets account for more than \(80\%\) of global construction machinery sales. Frost & Sullivan forecasts global construction machinery market sales of USD239.7bn in 2026, rising to USD279.8bn in 2028, implying a CAGR of \(8.5\%\), while China's construction machinery market sales are expected to increase from USD36.5bn to USD50.6bn over the same period. Although China offers greater cyclical upside, overseas markets remain much larger in absolute size, suggesting substantial room for Chinese construction machinery OEMs to expand abroad.

The global construction machinery market is also relatively concentrated. According to rankings published by KHL Group, the global industry's CR5 reached \(43.2\%\), with Caterpillar and Komatsu ranking first and second with market shares of \(15.9\%\) and \(11.2\%\), respectively. Chinese companies in the global top 20 include XCMG, Sany Heavy Industry, Zoomlion, and LiuGong, all of which are full-line domestic OEMs. Overall, we believe Chinese companies have already developed strong global competitiveness, but still have room to increase their overall share in overseas markets.

According to KHL's rankings, the world's top 50 construction machinery manufacturers generated total sales of USD237.6bn in 2024, of which leading Chinese companies contributed USD43.8bn. Based on this, we estimate that leading Chinese construction machinery companies had a combined overseas market share of around \(12\%\) in 2024, excluding the China market. The drivers of overseas expansion for Chinese construction machinery OEMs have evolved in recent years. As domestic growth has slowed and policy initiatives such as the Belt and Road Initiative and dual circulation have encouraged greater internationalization, overseas expansion has become a strategic priority for many Chinese industrial companies. For Chinese construction machinery companies, international expansion has evolved from a model that relied mainly on price advantages to one built on a broader set of competitive strengths, including supply chain efficiency, localized services, and electrification and intelligent equipment technologies. Since 2020, leading companies in the industry have generally seen a rapid increase in the revenue contribution from overseas business. Based on the current domestic and overseas gross margin profiles of OEMs, overseas business also generally carries higher gross margins than domestic business. We are positive on overseas markets becoming a core source of profitability for leading Chinese construction machinery companies.

For XCMG, we believe overseas expansion has become an increasingly important driver for both revenue growth and profitability improvement. On revenue, considering the company's continued overseas expansion and the upturn in China's domestic industry cycle, we conservatively assume that XCMG's overseas revenue contribution will increase by around 3pp per year over 2026-28F. Based on this assumption, we estimate that the company's overseas market share will rise from \(2.3\%\) in 2022 to \(5.4\%\) in 2028F. On profitability, XCMG's overseas gross margin has been significantly higher than its domestic gross margin over the long term. We assume its domestic gross margin will increase by 0.1pp per year over 2026-28F as the industry cycle improves. Based on the company's overall gross margin and domestic gross margin assumptions, we estimate that its overseas gross margin will continue to improve steadily to \(27.36\% / 28.58\% / 29.14\%\) in 2026/27/28F. As the revenue contribution from higher-margin overseas businesses continues to increase, we expect XCMG's profitability baseline to move higher steadily.

With domestic demand recovering and overseas markets continuing to expand, we expect the two demand drivers to reinforce each other and improve visibility on XCMG's earnings growth. Based on Frost & Sullivan's industry sales forecasts cited in Sany Heavy Industry's post-hearing information pack, together with our assumptions for XCMG's global market share across different business lines, we estimate revenue CAGRs of 17.8% and 8.0% for the company's earthmoving machinery and hoisting machinery businesses, respectively, over 2026-28F. To better illustrate the future growth drivers of each business line, we also forecast the concrete machinery business based on industry sales forecasts and global market share assumptions. We estimate XCMG's concrete machinery revenue at CNY9,846mn in 2025, and forecast a revenue CAGR of 12.0% for the segment over 2026-28F.

Mining machinery business: Building a second growth curve
In addition to its traditional construction machinery businesses, we believe mining machinery is likely to become an important medium- to long-term growth driver for XCMG.
Mining machinery demand entering a steady expansion phase, supported by energy-transition capex and equipment replacement

We believe mining machinery demand is on a steady uptrend, underpinned by several drivers. First, the energy transition is driving higher capex for key minerals such as copper, lithium and nickel, while global commodity and industrial metal prices remain relatively elevated. At the same time, overseas mining majors and resource-rich Belt and Road countries are showing stronger willingness to expand production, supporting incremental demand for mining equipment. Second, in China, mine consolidation toward larger-scale operations and stricter green mine policies, combined with the replacement cycle for existing equipment, are driving demand for electrified, large-scale and intelligent mining machinery. We believe the combination of overseas and domestic demand should support a continued upcycle in the mining machinery industry. According to Frost & Sullivan forecasts cited in Lingong Heavy Machinery's H-share prospectus, the global mining equipment market is expected to grow from CNY736.7bn in 2024 to CNY1,025.6bn in 2030, implying a CAGR of 5.7%; and China's mining equipment market is expected to expand from CNY123.0bn in 2024 to CNY177.1bn in 2030, implying a CAGR of 6.3%.

The commercial logic of mining machinery differs from that of general construction machinery, in our view. On the one hand, mining customers place greater emphasis on full-life-cycle aftermarket services, including spare parts, maintenance, and overhaul services. These businesses typically generate stronger customer stickiness and greater counter-cyclicality. For large mines, where equipment often runs around the clock, reliability and availability matter more than upfront price alone. In addition, mining equipment often requires customized services based on factors such as mine altitude and ore characteristics. Caterpillar and Komatsu have long dominated global mining machinery, particularly in the high-end segments, supported by early-mover advantages, proven technology and long operating track records with major mining customers.
Wide-body dump truck asset injection completes XCMG's mining machinery portfolio; integrated solution capability to drive share gains

Among domestic OEMs, XCMG has strong advantages in providing complete mining machinery solutions. On 31 May 2025, XCMG acquired a 51% stake in the group's heavy vehicle company, integrating businesses such as wide-body dump trucks and further strengthening the company's competitive advantage in complete and series-based mining machinery product offerings. In our view, the injection of the wide-body dump truck business should create synergies with XCMG's existing two-axle mining trucks, mining excavators, electric shovels and articulated dump trucks, enhancing its integrated “digging-loading-hauling” solution capability for open-pit mines.

Based on our assumptions for industry expansion and XCMG's market share gains, we forecast a \(33.7\%\) revenue CAGR for the company's mining machinery business over 2026-28F. According to the company's announcement on investor communication dated 4 February 2026, XCMG targets mining machinery revenue of more than CNY40bn by 2030, covering surface and underground mining equipment, spare parts, and related businesses. This compares with CNY9,377mn of mining machinery revenue in 2025, reflecting management's positive long-term outlook for the business. We believe the overall mining machinery segment has strong growth potential over the next few years. Conservatively, we assume XCMG's global market share in mining machinery will increase by 0.45pp/0.40pp/ 0.30pp in 2026-28F. Based on Frost & Sullivan's global mining equipment market size estimates discussed above, we forecast XCMG's mining machinery revenue at CNY13,553mn/CNY17,711mn/CNY22,428mn in 2026/27/28F.

SOE reform strengthens risk control and growth quality

We view SOE reform as a key driver of XCMG's improving operating quality in recent years. The company's reform path has followed a three-step strategy: mixed-ownership reform and strategic capital introduction, group-level listing, and equity incentives. XCMG launched mixed-ownership reform and strategic capital introduction in 2018, and completed its group-level listing in 2022. The listing brought a large number of high-quality assets into the listed company, including excavators, tower cranes, concrete machinery, and mining machinery. This filled product gaps in the listed company's portfolio and opened up new growth opportunities. During the industry downturn in 2022-25, XCMG still achieved steady net profit growth, supported by multi-segment synergies and overseas market expansion.

Following the reform, the company also strengthened its risk control awareness. In terms of bad debt risk, customer borrowings for which the company carried mortgage guarantee obligations stood at CNY10.099bn in 2022, while outstanding repurchase obligations under finance leases stood at CNY67.275bn. By 2025, these balances had declined to CNY9,706mn and CNY30,194mn, respectively, indicating a narrowing of the company's risk exposure. At the same time, XCMG's asset-liability ratio declined from \(68.78\%\) in 2022 to \(64.01\%\) in 2025, showing a steady improvement in its financial structure.

Equity incentives further align management with shareholders. In December 2025, XCMG announced an equity incentive plan, with a scale that set a new high for the A-share machinery sector. The plan uses three core assessment metrics: net profit, ROE, and operating cash flow. We believe this assessment framework emphasizes not only growth, but also the quality of growth. It should help drive XCMG's further transition from scale expansion to high-quality development.

Given XCMG's continued overseas expansion, steady earnings growth in recent years, and strong market positions across key product categories, we believe the company is well positioned to benefit from the current upcycle in China's construction machinery industry. We forecast total revenue of CNY115,734mn/CNY131,569mn/CNY147,567mn in 2026/27/28F, reflecting domestic recovery, overseas expansion and potential overseas demand disruption from geopolitical volatility in the Middle East. 1) Earthmoving machinery: We are constructive on XCMG's earthmoving machinery business. Domestic excavator and loader demand is recovering, overseas demand remains resilient, and XCMG continues to benefit from a competitive product offering and expanding global footprint. We forecast a 17.8% revenue CAGR for the segment over 2026-28F. The segment's gross margin increased slightly by 0.03pp in 2025. We expect the segment's gross margin to increase modestly by 0.3pp per year over 2026-28F, driven by continued overseas expansion, an industry recovery-led rebound in small- and mid-sized cranes, further electrification and smart upgrades, and disciplined cost control.

3) Concrete machinery: XCMG has been deeply engaged in the concrete machinery industry for years, with continuously improving core competitiveness. The company no longer disclosed concrete machinery as a separate segment in its 2025 annual report. Looking ahead, as XCMG continues to expand globally and domestic demand recovers, we forecast a revenue CAGR of \(12.0\%\) for the concrete machinery business over 2026-28F. In terms of profitability, supported by product premiumization and strict cost control, we assume the segment's gross margin will increase by 0.8pp/1.0pp/1.0pp in 2026/27/28F.

5) Other construction machinery equipment: This business mainly includes aerial work platforms, mining machinery, road machinery, and piling machinery, all of which are emerging businesses that XCMG is actively developing. Demand in the mining machinery industry is on a steady uptrend. XCMG has clear advantages in integrated, intelligent mining machinery solutions, supported by its years of overseas market development. Key downside risks

1) Changes in the global and regional competitive landscape: XCMG competes with both well-known multinational companies and domestic construction machinery manufacturers. The factors affecting industry competition are complex, while the construction machinery industry also faces changing market trends. The company therefore faces the risk of being unable to respond successfully to changes in the global and regional competitive landscape.

2) Weaker-than-expected R&D capabilities: If XCMG is unable to continue developing products that meet changing customer needs and mainstream industry trends, its product competitiveness could be constrained, which may adversely affect business development, profitability, and long-term growth prospects.

3) Slower-than-expected expansion of the mining machinery business: Demand for mining machinery is highly dependent on the capex plans of large overseas mining companies. A pullback in commodity prices, renewed inflationary pressure or tighter monetary policy in major economies could prompt mining companies to delay or scale back equipment replacement and expansion capex. This could slow the order conversion of XCMG's core mining products, such as mining trucks and large mining excavators, and put pressure on revenue growth.

4) Lower-than-expected downstream demand in China and overseas markets: If macroeconomic recovery falls short of expectations, downstream customer investment growth may continue to slow, which could weigh on sales of XCMG's products.

5) Complex global operating environment and geopolitical risks: International business is affected by political, cultural, human resource, and other factors. Overseas business expansion therefore involves a certain degree of uncertainty and risk.

6) Raw material price volatility: The cost of XCMG's raw materials and components may be affected by multiple factors, including market supply and demand, changes in suppliers, the availability of substitute materials, changes in supplier production conditions, and natural disasters.

7) FX volatility: As XCMG's overseas revenue contribution continues to increase, the company has a certain amount of business denominated in foreign currencies including the US dollar, euro, and Japanese yen. Significant FX fluctuations may affect the company's earnings.
